summary: Jiryo Masuda was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Unrai Wogihara (attested 1930). He later served as a professor at the University of Calcutta and taught Prabodh Chandra Bagchi.

Jitendra Nath Banerjea (1895–1966) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied under Hemchandra Raychaudhuri around 1916–1918, taught Sarasi Kumar Saraswati, and served as Carmichael Professor of Ancient Indian History and Culture at the University of Calcutta (~1952–1959).

Jitendra Nath Mohanty (1928–2023) was an Indologist and philosopher educated at Presidency University (B.A.), Calcutta (M.A.), and Göttingen (Ph.D.). He taught at Calcutta, Burdwan, The New School, Oklahoma, Emory, and was a professor at Temple University (~1986–2011).
Jitsushyu Oshika (b. 1919) is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tohoku University and later held a professorship at Toyo University, attested in 1980–1981.

Jitsuzo Kuwabara (1871–1931) was a sinologist and historian who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1892–1896). He held posts at the Third Higher School (1898–1899), Tokyo Higher Normal School (1899–1907), and Kyoto Imperial University (1909–1930).
Jiun Kubota (b. 1932) is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under traditional teacher Kōun Yamada from around 1970 to 1989 and subsequently succeeded him.

Jiyu Ren (1916–2009) studied at Peking University under Lin He and Yongtong Tang. A scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhism, he taught at Peking University (1942–1964) and directed the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences and Chinese Academy of Sciences.

Jiyu-Kennett (1924–1996) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar educated at Durham, Trinity Laban, and Soji-ji. She was head priest at Unpuku-ji (~1968–1969) and founded Shasta Abbey in 1969, serving as abbess until 1996.

Joachim Gentz is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. He served as Junior Professor in Religious Studies at the University of Göttingen and as Reader in Chinese Studies at the University of Edinburgh (attested 2013).

Joachim Heinrich Campe (1746–1818) was a linguist who studied at the University of Helmstedt (~1765–1768) and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1768–1769). He also taught Wilhelm von Humboldt.
Joachim Prandstetter is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He earned his Magister at the University of Vienna in 1994, where he studied under Gerhard Oberhammer.

Joachim Wach (1898–1955) studied at Leipzig, Munich, Berlin, Freiburg, and Heidelberg. A religious studies and philosophy scholar, he taught at Leipzig (1924–1935), Brown University (1935–1946), and chaired the History of Religions at the University of Chicago Divinity School (1945–1955).

Joan Jiko Halifax (b. 1942) works in Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at Newcomb, Tulane, and Union Institute (PhD), she held posts at Columbia, Maryland Psychiatric Research Center, and Miami, and later founded the Ojai Foundation and Upaya Zen Center.

Joanna Gottfried Williams (1939–2022) was an Indologist and art historian educated at Swarthmore College, Radcliffe College, and Harvard University. She served on the faculty as a professor at the University of California, Berkeley from around 1971 to 2007.

Joanna Macy (1929–2025) was a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. She completed her studies at Wellesley College (~1946–1950) and Syracuse University (~1973–1978), and she taught Stephanie Kaza and Doug Kraft.

Joanne Punzo Waghorne is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied at the University of Chicago (~1970–1976). She held posts at UMass Boston, Bowdoin College, UNC Chapel Hill (1987–2002), and Syracuse University.

Joe Bransford Wilson is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Wisconsin-Madison and the University of Virginia (Ph.D. 1984). He taught at Virginia (1981–1985) and became Associate Professor of Asian Philosophy and Religion at UNC Wilmington (attested 1994–2001).

Joe Cribb (b. 1947) is a scholar of numismatics, archaeology, and Indology educated at Queen Mary University of London. He was Keeper of Coins and Medals at the British Museum (1970–2010) and held leadership roles in the Royal and Oriental Numismatic Societies.
Joey Hung (b. 1991) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the Hong Kong Academy for Performing Arts. Hung has held an academic post at the Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts.
Jogendra Singh is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He pursued his education at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara, where he studied under Uma Shankar Vyas.
